These data show that the mechanism of softening of an alloy is controlled by the density of the dislocations over which the diffusion occurs.
This indicates that particles of the ?,'-phase have a high coagulation rate at 650- 750°C, which leads to earlier softening of the specimens subjected to TMT.
For low-alloyed alloys of the EI437B type this is associated with the development of recrystallization at operating temperatures of 650 - 750°C.
